algorithm.argument: rdi = the allocator object (called 'this' here); no other argument register is read
algorithm.entry_formula: entry = array + index * 64 (u64 add), returned in rax; the entry itself is never dereferenced by this routine
algorithm.fallback_path: selector negative: the seed callee's word is advanced by one step (see fallback_step) and the NEW word becomes the selector; the step and the store back happen before the shared index computation
algorithm.fallback_step: t = seed * 16807 in 64 bits from the zero-extended 32-bit word; s = (t & 0x7fffffff) + (t >> 31) as a 32-bit sum; when the sum's sign bit is set, s -= 0x7fffffff (cmovs on the add's flags). This is the Park-Miller minimal-standard step mod 2^31-1 for every seed except that a sum of exactly 0x7fffffff has no sign bit, so seed 0x7fffffff maps to itself instead of to 0; seed 0 also maps to itself
algorithm.fast_path: selector >= 0: the selector is used verbatim as a u32; the seed word is neither read nor written
algorithm.index_formula: index = selector & mask, mask = (1 << (shift & 31)) - 1 from a 32-bit shl/sub pair on ebx; the count is the +0x50 dword's low 5 bits, so shift 32 wraps the mask to 0 and shift 33 gives mask 1
algorithm.tls_store: the qword at fs:0 - 0x408 receives index | (1 << (shift & 63)): the bts count is the +0x50 dword's low 6 bits, twice the width of the mask count, and the bit is never inside the index (the mask leaves it clear), so the stored value is index + 2^(shift & 63). fs:0 is loaded first (the TCB self pointer) and the slot is addressed as that pointer - 0x408

callees_by_contract.0x60d5cd0: CPUID selector, FDE 0x60d5cd0..0x60d5cf0: returns CPUID leaf-1 EBX bits 31:24 (the initial APIC id) as a non-negative int, or -1 when CPUID leaf 0 reports maximum leaf 0. Called once at 0x605e17b; internals pinned from its own window bytes for this contract line only, it is not modelled
callees_by_contract.0x61c4080: per-thread seed-word getter, FDE 0x61c4080..0x61c4117: returns a pointer to a per-thread 32-bit word, lazily initialised from a hash of the thread identity; 17 direct callers. Called once at 0x605e1d0 on the fallback path only; this routine reads the word, advances it and stores it back. Internals not modelled

consumers.argument_forwarding: both call sites pass the caller's own rdi (the allocator object) unchanged
consumers.sites: 0x5f11931 in the shard AllocateAligned window 0x5f117a0..0x5f11c38 and 0x5f11cf7 in the outer Allocate window 0x5f11c40..0x5f12162; per the two consumer packets, the call runs when the selected shard's lock byte is set and again when a LOCK CMPXCHG on an entry lock loses its race; the return value becomes the caller's shard entry and the caller then spins on that entry's lock

object_layout.array_0x48: qword at this + 0x48: the shard array base; each entry is 64 bytes, which is the shl $0x6 in the entry formula
object_layout.shift_0x50: dword at this + 0x50: read as a dword by both paths (mov 0x50(%rbp),%r12d). Only its low 6 bits are observable: bits 0..4 feed the 32-bit mask count (& 31 via cl), bits 0..5 feed the bts count (& 63). The consumer packets describe the field as a byte; nothing in this window reads the upper three bytes except through those masked counts
object_layout.tls_selector_slot: qword at fs:0 - 0x408: the same TLS slot the consumer packets document as the allocator's cpuid slot (their windows reach it through the TLS getter _ZTHN7rocksdb15ConcurrentArena9tls_cpuidE); this routine writes it directly, without the getter

unknowns: why the stored TLS value marks the index with the 2^(shift & 63) bit; the consumer packets read the slot as a plain cpuid value, so the bit's consumer-side role is not established by this window
whether the +0x50 dword's upper three bytes are ever nonzero in practice; both counts mask them away, so this window cannot distinguish a byte field stored in a dword slot from a true dword field

whether the fallback seed word is shared with the seed callee's other 16 callers' purposes (e.g. hash-state keys) or dedicated to shard selection; this window only observes the read/advance/store of its first dword
the exact source-level identity of the routine (the ConcurrentArena association is inference from the consumer packets' TLS symbol and object layout, not from anything inside this window)
unwind: FDE .eh_frame offset 0x3677d0, length 0x2c, CIE at section offset 0x0 with augmentation "zR"; the FDE augmentation data length is 0, so there is no LSDA pointer and no landing pad in the window (the two calls are to callees the frame treats as non-throwing for this body). The window saves r12/rbp/rbx and restores them on the single ret at 0x605e1c6; the fallback block at 0x605e1d0 sits after that ret and inside the FDE range, reached only by the entry js.
